title: Max Content Length (Textable, Numeric)
documentation:
## Purpose
Limits the number of characters or tokens of document content passed to a machine. Used to prevent oversized inputs from exceeding downstream capacity.

## When to use
Apply this parameter on ingestion or preprocessing machines that must truncate or split content before forwarding it. It complements [Max Context Length](https://capdag.com/browse/media:max-context-length;inference;limit;operator;model;textable;numeric), which governs the model's total window.

## Notes
Valid range: 256–131072. Content exceeding this limit should be chunked using [Chunk Size](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-size;textable;numeric) rather than silently truncated.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
